set_aside.subject: Bootstrap administrator success output
set_aside.text: “the success message shows the normalized email” does not define the email-normalization rule whose result is now observable
set_aside.question: Exactly how is the submitted bootstrap email normalized before uniqueness checks, storage, and display in the success message?
options: Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the entire address
Trim and canonicalize only the domain while preserving the local part
Apply Unicode or IDNA canonicalization in addition to case and whitespace rules
set_aside.default_guess: Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the entire address using the same normalization used for staff login identifiers.

events: The host operator submits ` User@Example.COM ` and a valid password to the bootstrap command.
The command creates the administrator and prints its success message.
outcomes: The operator sees `User@example.com` or another canonical form.
witness.observer: The host operator and any deployment automation capturing the success output.

set_aside.subject: Viewer access-link entry
set_aside.text: “entry is rate limited” names no limiting subject, threshold, time window, persistence rule, or observable refusal
set_aside.question: What events consume the viewer-entry limit, what identity or network attribute is limited, over what window, and what response and recovery behavior occurs when the limit is exceeded?
options: Limit by access-link credential or viewer identity
set_aside.default_guess: Use combined per-IP and per-credential limits, count failed entry attempts, and return a concealed temporary refusal with a defined retry interval.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid access link and shares a public IP address with other users.
events: Another actor makes many failed viewer-entry attempts from that shared IP using unrelated link values.
The viewer then follows the valid access link from the same IP.
outcomes: A per-IP limiter refuses the valid viewer entry.
A per-credential limiter accepts the valid viewer entry because its credential has no failed attempts.
witness.observer: The viewer attempting to enter the portal.

set_aside.subject: Manual budget created by archived-project progress read
set_aside.text: “creates that empty manual budget version” does not say whether the new version becomes the active budget version or remains inactive
set_aside.question: What activation state does the automatically created empty manual budget version receive, both when the project has no active budget and when another budget version is already active?
options: Always create it active, replacing any active version
Activate it only when the project has no active budget; otherwise leave it inactive
set_aside.default_guess: Activate it only when no budget version is active, and otherwise create it inactive without changing the existing active version.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version and no active budget version.
events: An authorized staff member reads the project's progress list.
The read creates the empty manual budget version.
A permitted viewer subsequently reads the project's budget summary.
outcomes: The viewer sees an active manual budget with no sections.
The viewer is told that no active budget is available because the created manual version is inactive.
witness.observer: The staff member reading progress and the viewer reading the budget.

set_aside.subject: Presentation of an automatically created empty manual budget
set_aside.text: The new empty manual budget exception does not reconcile the created record with “Unavailable data is shown explicitly, never fabricated or replaced by silent zeros”
set_aside.question: After the progress read creates an empty manual budget version, do budget and derived-value reads treat it as a valid empty budget, as unavailable budget data, or as a distinct initialized-but-empty state?
options: Return a valid manual budget whose section list and totals are empty or zero
Continue reporting budget and derived values as unavailable
Expose a distinct initialized-but-empty status without presenting financial zeros
set_aside.default_guess: Expose a distinct initialized-but-empty manual budget and keep financial and progress values unavailable until planned sections exist.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version, sections, expenses, or planned work.
events: An authorized staff member reads its progress list, creating the empty manual budget version.
A viewer with an existing grant reads the budget summary and overall progress.
outcomes: The viewer sees a manual budget with zero totals and zero or empty progress.
The viewer sees budget and progress as unavailable, possibly with an explicit empty-budget status.

set_aside.subject: Concurrent archived-project progress reads
set_aside.text: “when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version” does not define concurrent get-or-create behavior or a duplicate-creation failure
set_aside.question: If multiple authorized progress-list reads simultaneously observe that no manual budget version exists, must they converge on one version, and what does each read return if creation races?
options: Atomically create exactly one version and let every read succeed against it
Create one version but fail one or more racing reads with a conflict or storage error
set_aside.default_guess: Enforce one manual version atomically and let all racing reads succeed against the same created version.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version.
events: Two authorized staff members issue progress-list reads concurrently.
Both requests initially observe that no manual budget version exists.
outcomes: Exactly one manual budget version is created and both reads succeed.
Two versions are created, or one read fails because the other created the version first.
witness.observer: The two staff members and later users reading or maintaining the project's budget.
